ghats.name: Ramkund
ghats.historical_note: Nashik's principal Shahi Snan bathing ghat, believed associated with Lord Rama's exile. Immediately adjacent to the Kalaram Mandir corridor - see kalaram_marg below for the 2003 stampede site.

ghats.name: Kalaram Mandir Marg (approach lane)
ghats.location: Panchavati, Nashik - the lane connecting Kalaram Mandir to Ramkund
ghats.historical_note: Site of the August 27, 2003 Nashik Kumbh stampede: a barricade at a gully near Kalaram Mandir gave way under crowd pressure as sadhus threw coins to devotees, killing 39 and injuring roughly 150. Roads here are documented as narrower than 6 feet (~1.8m) at several points. Source: Al Jazeera, 'Indian stampede leaves 39 dead' (2003); Tribune India coverage, Aug 28, 2003.

ghats.name: Kushavarta Ghat
ghats.historical_note: The symbolic origin point of the Godavari river; the primary Shahi Snan ghat at Trimbakeshwar, directly adjacent to the Trimbakeshwar Jyotirlinga temple.

ghats.name: Panchavati Godavari Ghat corridor
ghats.location: Panchavati, Nashik (Godavari riverfront, downstream of Ramkund)
ghats.historical_note: Secondary riverfront bathing corridor used to relieve Ramkund overflow during peak Shahi Snan windows.
